summary.headline: NIIT Q2 FY27 revenue fell 6% YoY to INR982 million on GSI consumption pullback; EBITDA turned positive at INR27 million (2.7% margin).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR982 million, down 6% YoY but up 3% QoQ, and H1 revenue of INR1,939 million grew 3% YoY, below management's earlier projections. The shortfall was driven by a sharp QoQ compression in GSI consumption, with four of the largest GSI clients down as much as INR100 million YoY. Cost cuts (operating expenses down 8% YoY) lifted EBITDA to INR27 million, but a net loss of INR22 million was recorded after lower treasury income and an exceptional legal cost. Management now assumes FY27 revenue will be broadly flat and expects a low single-digit EBITDA margin for the year.

segments.name: Enterprise BIPS (BFSI and Industry Performance Programs)
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR200 million, up 17% YoY and 66% QoQ; BIPS segment revenue overall INR321 million, up 11% YoY.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR357 million, up 3% YoY, with uniform growth across technology and BFSI portfolios.

segments.name: AI-led revenue
segments.commentary: Share of revenue directly attributable to AI rose to 12.4% from 9% in the prior quarter; AI coaches are sold on subscription on top of training fees.

guidance_outlook: Revenue for the rest of FY27 assumed broadly flat, based on Q2 experience; to be revisited next quarter.
Low single-digit EBITDA margin expected to continue for the full year.
GSI volumes expected to remain under pressure for the next two quarters; no significant recovery expected in that window.
Capex expected to stay moderated in coming quarters unless a large initiative emerges.
New CEO Anish Sarkar to review portfolio, go-to-market, and cost structure over the next 60 to 90 days as part of the FY planning cycle.
capex_capacity: Capex INR44 million in Q2 FY27, down from INR69 million a year ago; management says many earlier AI and digital projects are now being capitalised.
Investment in sales team and AI offerings to continue, with inorganic opportunities evaluated for capabilities, channels or IP.

RPS Consulting, NIIT StackRoute and NIIT Enterprise Solutions being integrated into a single Enterprise Technology Learning Solutions (ETLS) unit; benefits on fixed cost expected over the next few quarters.
demand_pricing: GSI consumption fell QoQ in a quarter that is traditionally strong; four largest GSI clients were down as much as INR100 million YoY, reflecting in-sourcing and cost pressure.
Order intake INR1,301 million; 10 new logos added (three technology, three higher education, four BIPS).
Selected as learning transformation partner by a top Indian bank; revenue impact expected in future quarters.
Two large banks engaged to set up wealth and sales academies using AI simulations and AI coaches.
Enterprise technology versus BFSI/industry mix about 67:33; management expects it to remain around two-thirds technology.
Enrollment around 220,000 in the quarter (per management on call).

qa_highlights.question: Is the headcount reduction driven by demand weakness or by AI productivity gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is both: AI efficiencies (development productivity up 50%+), lower sales and back-office costs, and lower volumes. Headcount reduction is not expected to continue at this pace, but trimming will happen as needed.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the technology versus BFSI mix settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly two-thirds technology and one-third BFSI and other industries, give or take a few points. Enterprise BFSI and industry demand is seen as growing as AI adoption rises.

qa_highlights.question: Are investments largely complete, and can margins improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is moderated and many projects are now capitalised. Management said AI remains a moving target and investment will continue, but at lower levels unless a large initiative arises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the benefit of integrating RPS Consulting, StackRoute and NIIT Enterprise Solutions?
qa_highlights.answer: Combining sales teams has given focused coverage and a broader solution set. Fixed-cost benefits are expected over the next few quarters, as integration costs take time to settle.

qa_highlights.question: Can new sectors such as manufacturing or EV offset the slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing and EV are work-in-progress initiatives with a team in place. Management said revenue would be disclosed once it becomes significant, and that capital-intensive clients face rate and energy pressure, so results will take time.

risks_watch: Further GSI consumption cuts or in-sourcing by large GSI clients; recovery not expected for two quarters.
Revenue guidance of broadly flat for FY27 leaves limited room for growth; next quarter's revision is pending.
Treasury income volatility from interest-rate mark-to-market, which swung profit between quarters (INR175 million in Q1 to INR41 million in Q2).
Receivable days rose to 63 from 53, linked to delayed collections that management says were received in October.
Leadership transition and the integration of the RPS, StackRoute and Enterprise Solutions businesses may affect execution.
summary.management_tone: Candid about the Q2 miss and cautious on the next two quarters, but confident on the BIPS, AI and cost-control story. Management was less specific on GSI recovery timing and on new-sector revenue.
key_quotes: This compression in spend in a certain sense, was secular across some of these large clients, and there are many theories to it, but one of them could be that they had lower numbers of onboarding
Enterprise BIPS achieved an all -time high revenue of INR200 million and a strong growth of 17% Y-o-Y with 66% quarter-on-quarter.
we are, at this point of time, looking at the rest of the year and going by the experience of this quarter, assuming that the revenue is likely to be broadly flat.

growth.why: Management now assumes FY27 revenue broadly flat (cut from earlier projections), with low single-digit EBITDA margin held; backing is partial: order intake INR1,301m, 10 new logos, a bank learning partnership and cost actions, but no specific capacity, and GSI volumes are guided to stay under pressure for two more quarters.

mgmt.note: New CEO Anish Sarkar will review portfolio, go-to-market and cost structure over the next 60 to 90 days as part of the FY planning cycle; no specific growth targets stated yet.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 2.7% (INR27m) after Q1 was negative INR14m, and opex fell 8% YoY, but management guides only a low single-digit EBITDA margin for FY27 and integration benefits are 'over the next few quarters'.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or branches discussed; capex was cut to INR44m from INR69m YoY and management says capex will stay moderated unless a large initiative emerges.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Enterprise revenue fell 11% YoY and technology programs fell 13% YoY on GSI pullback; management expects GSI volumes to stay under pressure for two quarters, though BIPS grew 17% YoY and 10 new logos were added.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is moderated at INR44m a quarter and many AI and digital projects are now capitalised, so a new capex announcement is not signalled, and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to broadly flat from earlier projections and H1 revenue grew only 3% YoY, with the guidance to be revisited next quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management already cut FY27 revenue to broadly flat, GSI recovery is not expected for two quarters, and receivable days rose to 63 from 53, so further cuts are possible if GSI pressure persists.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI-led revenue rose to 12.4% of revenue from 9% and AI coaches are sold on subscription, but no specific new product launch date was given; manufacturing and EV initiatives are still work-in-progress with revenue undisclosed.

rows.label: Bank learning partnership and wealth/sales academies
rows.why: Order intake was INR1,301m with a top Indian bank selected as learning transformation partner and two large banks engaged for AI-simulation academies, though the revenue timing was not quantified.

rows.label: Headcount and fixed-cost integration (ETLS)
rows.why: Headcount fell 50 QoQ and 124 YoY to 816, and merging RPS, StackRoute and Enterprise Solutions is expected to bring fixed-cost benefits over the next few quarters, though management said the headcount pace will not continue.

rows.label: New CEO portfolio and cost review
rows.why: CEO Anish Sarkar is reviewing portfolio, go-to-market and cost structure within 60-90 days, which could reset guidance and cost base next quarter.

tone.note: Management was candid about the Q2 miss and cautious on GSI recovery, which it sees taking two quarters, but confident on BIPS, AI and cost control. Analysts pressed on the GSI decline, the flat FY27 revenue assumption and the timing of new-sector revenue.
